description:
Context
We need a standardized, repeatable benchmark workload suite that the org can use to:
- set/validate Dedicated tier baseline throughput targets by shape
- catch regressions in runtime/scheduler changes
- make Sales/PM numbers defensible (and comparable across regions)

Right now benchmark runs are inconsistent across owners (different prompt mixes, different concurrency ramp, warmup handling varies, streaming toggles differ). This creates churn in tier threshold discussions and makes it hard to interpret variance.

This issue scopes the benchmark suite + CI/perf-canary coverage that becomes the source of truth for tier baseline workloads.

Goals
- Define a small set of canonical "tier baseline" scenarios (input/output length distributions + concurrency + streaming settings).
- Encode scenarios into perf-canary and make them runnable per shape/model.
- Standardize run protocol: warmup, measurement window, exclusions, and what artifacts must be captured.
- Add regression thresholds + reporting so runtime changes that degrade throughput trigger investigation before rollout.

Non-goals
- No bespoke customer workload modeling in this ticket (handled case-by-case via perf engagements).
- Not building a full benchmark UI; output is CLI + artifacts (JSON/CSV) + Grafana/CI annotations.
- Not changing the primary SLI definition here (must align to ADR-0127 + measurement standard).

Proposed canonical scenarios (v1)
All scenarios use the Dedicated throughput measurement standard windowing and exclusions (warmup excluded; maintenance excluded; customer-induced 4xx excluded).

Scenario A: "Chat/short" (prefill-light, decode-heavy)
- Purpose: representative of most chatbots / SaaS copilots
- Input tokens (p50/p95): ~256 / ~1k
- Output tokens: fixed 256 (or capped at 256) to reduce long-tail variance
- Streaming: ON
- Tools/function calling: OFF
- Concurrency: fixed per tier (see below)

Scenario B: "Chat/long-context" (prefill-heavy)
- Purpose: stress prefill + KV cache behavior; catches regressions in prefill kernels and scheduler fairness
- Input tokens (p50/p95): ~2k / ~6k (bounded by model context)
- Output tokens: fixed 128
- Streaming: ON
- Concurrency: fixed per tier

Scenario C: "Mixed" (realistic distribution)
- Purpose: guard against over-optimizing a single distribution
- Input tokens: weighted mix of short/medium/long (document exact weights in perf-canary config)
- Output tokens: mix of 64/128/256
- Streaming: ON
- Concurrency: fixed per tier

Tier concurrency mapping (for benchmark purposes)
NOTE: these are benchmark parameters used to derive/validate tier baselines; not necessarily the customer-facing concurrency guarantee.
- Standard baseline: 8 concurrent streams
- Performance baseline: 16 concurrent streams
- Premium baseline: 32 concurrent streams

(If SRE/PM prefers different numbers, keep the suite flexible via config but pin the defaults so we can compare week-over-week.)

Models + shapes coverage (v1)
- Models: pick 2–3 representative Redwood-catalog models used in Dedicated:
  - 8B-class instruct
  - 70B-class instruct
  - optional: MoE model if it’s in the Dedicated catalog and materially changes scheduler behavior
- Shapes: cover each tier-supported GPU family (e.g., L4, A100, H100) with 1–2 canonical shapes each.

Run protocol (must be codified in suite)
- Warmup: N minutes or N requests (explicit), excluded from measurement
- Measurement: steady-state window (explicit) aligned to measurement standard
- Ramp: avoid step-change spikes; use a short ramp to target concurrency
- Record:
  - effective output tok/s (primary)
  - request completion rate
  - queue depth statistics
  - throttling rate / admission control events (once ENG-2206 lands)
  - p50/p95 TTFT and decode latency (secondary for diagnosis)
- Environment capture:
  - runtime version / git SHA
  - model version / quantization profile
  - GPU type/count, driver, CUDA, NCCL
  - MIG on/off
  - region + zone

Implementation plan
1) Spec alignment (done in doc, then encode)
- Confirm scenario definitions with PM (Lauren) + SRE (Rafael/Aisha).
- Confirm we’re using the same tokenization/token counting method as the throughput SLI.

2) perf-canary scenarios
- Add scenario configs for A/B/C with a shared schema:
  - prompt generator
  - length distribution
  - target concurrency
  - run durations (warmup + measure)
  - output caps
- Ensure scenarios can be invoked per model/shape in CI and on-demand.

3) Regression thresholds + gating
- Define initial thresholds (soft fail / hard fail):
  - hard fail if effective tok/s drops > X% vs last known good for same model+shape+scenario
  - soft fail if drop > Y% with an issue automatically filed/tagged
- Thresholds should be tuned to observed variance; start conservative and tighten after 2 weeks of data.

4) Artifacts + reporting
- Save structured artifacts (JSON/CSV) to CI and to a shared bucket path used by dashboards.
- Post a summary comment into Linear (or CI annotation) including:
  - deltas vs baseline
  - links to artifacts
  - suspected phase (prefill vs decode) when regressions occur (based on spans/metrics)

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Scenarios A/B/C defined in perf-canary with pinned defaults + documented in README.
- [ ] Single command can run a scenario locally against a Dedicated deployment (or staging) and produce artifacts.
- [ ] CI job exists that runs at least Scenario A nightly on one representative model/shape and reports deltas.
- [ ] Regression detection: creates an annotated CI failure (hard) and/or Linear issue (soft) with artifacts.
- [ ] Baseline numbers are published (in the benchmark results sheet) for v1 shapes/models with a clear timestamp and runtime SHA.
- [ ] PM/SRE sign-off that suite aligns with the throughput measurement standard (windowing/exclusions).

Open questions
- Token counting: do we count "output tokens" as post-tokenizer tokens only, or include special tokens/stop tokens? Must match gateway SLI emission.
- Streaming semantics: confirm we treat streaming as normal completion (avoid biasing by client consumption). For canary, client will read stream fully.
- Long-context upper bounds: cap long-context scenario based on model context and avoid OOM variance.
- Variance management: how many iterations per run are required before we trust the delta?

Risks / trade-offs
- Overfitting: a too-narrow scenario may drive runtime changes that improve benchmarks but not real traffic. Mitigate with Scenario C.
- Noise: GPU neighbor effects / thermal throttling can cause false positives. Mitigate by widening thresholds initially and capturing node-level telemetry.
- Cardinality: attaching model+scenario+shape labels everywhere can explode metrics. Prefer artifact-based baselines + small set of dashboard labels.

Notes
- This ticket is intentionally scoped to benchmark suite standardization + canary coverage. Tier thresholds themselves are defined in PM-482 and justified using results from this suite + the baseline sheet.

2025-01-29 (Aisha Bello): From SRE side: please pin measurement window to match SLO tooling (recommend 10m steady-state) and explicitly exclude first N minutes warmup. Also capture throttling once admission control lands (ENG-2206), but don’t block this ticket on it.

2025-02-03 (Omar El-Sayed): Implemented scenario schema in perf-canary branch; added prompt generator knobs for length distributions. Pending review on whether we standardize tokenization by calling runtime tokenizer vs offline tokenizer.

2025-02-06 (Sofia Ivanova): Re: tokenization—prefer using the same token accounting emitted by gateway SLI (ENG-2194). If not possible, document delta explicitly and keep canary comparisons consistent (same method week-over-week).

2025-02-10 (Omar El-Sayed): Opened perf-canary PR with tier baseline scenarios and artifact output. Next: add nightly job on one H100 shape + 70B model; will coordinate with Vanessa for a stable canary pool.

2025-02-14 (Sergio Costa): Once artifacts land in shared bucket, I can add a lightweight Grafana panel that plots nightly effective tok/s by scenario (no high-cardinality labels, just scenario+shape+model for the canary set).
